title.narrative: Green Al-Salt: Public Spaces and Living Heritage for Socio-Economic Development

description.narrative:
In 2021, UNESCO inscribed Al-Salt city as a World Heritage Site, branding it “The Place of Tolerance and Urban Hospitality”. Over the centuries, this city has embraced diverse communities in its dense urban fabric, and its public spaces have stood as networks linking homes, faiths, and cultures, preserving a legacy of tolerance and coexistence. Rooted in its socio-cultural architectural and urban features, Al-Salt weave intangible attributes like urban hospitality, unique craftsmanship, and cohabitation with tangible elements such as urban spaces. However, these public spaces, vital for fostering tolerance and social cohesion, now confront multiple challenges, including drainage issues, vandalism, and deteriorating infrastructure. The integrity of Al-Salt is vulnerable, demanding the conservation and rejuvenation of these spaces and their associated living heritage assets to uphold its hospitable urban character. Yet, as the city continues to grow amid evolving challenges, such as a pandemic, the influx of refugees, rising unemployment, and the effects of climate change, public spaces' significance remains unparalleled yet increasingly overlooked, risking the integrity and social cohesion of this historically and culturally significant city. Notably, the growth in tourism since the WH inscription poses both an opportunity and a challenge, straining an already densely populated city while presenting prospects for local economic growth via heritage valorization.
Accordingly, this project aims to enhance the social cohesion, increase the livelihood opportunities, and maintain the integrity of Al-Salt City through the revitilization of public spaces as well as the valorisation of living heritage assets. The project adopts a multi-dimensional approach that is informed by the urban development pressures and challenges that threaten the vulnerable sustainability, authenticity, and cohesion of the urban fabric of Al-Salt city. These open public spaces connecting the historically significant buildings act as the city’s heart, bringing life to social and economic relations, and creating a unique network that connects diverse cultures, religions, and communities to maintain social cohesion. Therefore, the revitalization, rehabilitation, and conservation of public spaces is a national priority that will maintain the already-vulnerable integrity of the historical city of Al-Salt. This will allow for cultural expressions, such as art and food, to be valorised for income generation, in the endeavour to prevent the future loss of ICH practices and traditions and improve the livelihoods of vulnerable communities.
The proposed intervention will begin with and be informed by the UN-Habitat Public Space City-Wide Assessment and the implemented pilot projects will be informed by the UN-Habitat Public Space Site-Specific Assessments findings and analysis. The physical dimensions of public spaces, and the historical links to Al-Salt’s outstanding universal values, will be incorporated into this assessment and in turn inform a conservation-based response. The intangible cultural heritage (ICH) aspects will be mapped through a new methodology developed by UNESCO for the inventorying of intangible heritage in urban areas and piloted in nine urban areas, including in the city of Irbid, in different regions of the world.
